etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English lovely, luvelich, lufli, from Old English luflīċ, luflīc (“amiable, loving, lovable”), equivalent to love +‎ -ly.

definitions.definition: Beautiful; charming; very pleasing in form, looks, tone, or manner.

quote.citation: 1915, Herman Cyril McNeile, The Lieutenant and Others:
1923 October, Robert Frost, “[Grace Notes.] Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening.”, in New Hampshire […], New York, N.Y.: Henry Holt and Company, →OCLC, page 87:
quote.text: The woods are lovely, dark and deep.

quote.citation: 1977, Skip Scarborough, Bill Withers (lyrics and music), “Lovely Day”, performed by Bill Withers:
quote.text: Then I look at you / And the world's alright with me / Just one look at you / And I know it's gonna be / A lovely day

quote.citation: 1891, Thomas Hardy, Tess of the d'Urbervilles, volume 1, London: James R. Osgood, McIlvaine and Co., page 135:
quote.text: It is a lovely night, and why should we not prolong our ride a little?"

quote.citation: c. 1595–1596 (date written), William Shakespeare, “A Midsommer Nights Dreame”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies: Published According to the True Originall Copies (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act I, scene ii]:

c. 1590–1592 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Taming of the Shrew”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act III, scene ii]:
quote.text: seal the title with a lovely kiss

definitions.definition: (informal) An attractive, lovely person, especially a (professional) beauty.

quote.citation: 1969, Peter Sarstedt (lyrics and music), “Where Do You Go To (My Lovely)?”:
quote.text: But where do you go to my lovely / When you're alone in your bed?

quote.citation: 2011, Theodora Floros, What'S for Lunch?: A Cooking Guide for Parents, →ISBN, page 13:
quote.text: In Montréal, the summer months bring in a huge variety of fruits and vegetables and this is the time to preserve them. Preserving can also refer to the storage of these fiber and vitamin rich lovelies.
May Bell ironed the last ruffle and then hung the dress in the wardrobe next to her other lovelies.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English lovely, luveliche, from Old English luflīċe (“lovingly, amiably, kindly, dearly, with good will or love, willingly”), equivalent to love +‎ -ly.

definitions.definition: (informal) In a lovely fashion or manner; beautifully.

quote.citation: 2014, Neil Bartlett, chapter 18, in The Disappearance Boy‎[1], A&C Black:
quote.text: She's not everyone's cup of tea, what with the way she speaks her mind and doesn't always do her hair in the morning, but she scrubs up lovely.

etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English lofly, lovely (“praiseworthy; laudatory”), equivalent to lofe +‎ -ly. Cognate with Dutch loffelijk (“laudable, praiseworthy”), German löblich (“commendable, laudable, praiseworthy”), Swedish lovlig (“permissible”). More at lofe, love.

quote.citation: 1773, Thomas Boston (the Elder.), Alexander Colden, The Whole Works of the late reverend and learned Mr. Thomas Boston, Minister of the Gospel at Etterick:
quote.text: And so he is in the eyes of all who live to his praise. To them every attribute of God is lovely. The holiness and purity of his nature is most lovely to them.
He is altogether lovely. O, all our praises of him are poor and low things!

quote.citation: 1823, Church of England, Llyfr gweddi gyffredin:
quote.text: О praise the Lord, for the Lord is gracious : О sing praises unto his Name, for it is lovely.

quote.citation: 1834, David Dickson, A Brief Explication of the Psalms - Volume 1, page 39:
quote.text: It is the duty of all believers to join themselves cheerfully in the setting forth the Lord's care over them, and whatsoever may make his lovely Majesty known to the world: for so he requireth the present precept and example, -- sing praises to the Lord.

quote.citation: 1876, John Vaughan, Trinity hymns for the worship of the three-one Jehovah in faith & love:
quote.text: My precious Saviour's matchless name ; He's wise and holy, just and true, And altogether lovely too.
